summary: Okanogan County, WA lookout built 1933 as a log cabin on an 84-ft pole tower; removed 1958. Summit is now mining-company land posted no trespassing.

facts.design: Log cabin on an 84-foot pole tower with an L-6 cab; ladder access only, no stairs
facts.status_note: Removed in 1958; sources describe footings and foundation pieces, not a standing tower

access.note: Summit is owned by a mining company and posted no trespassing, per WillhiteWeb

visit.trail_note: No tower remains to climb. The summit is posted private land. WillhiteWeb describes Forest Service roads that stop within a quarter mile of the top, and says the summit is gated and signed no trespassing.

events.note: Aug 2, 1929 storm started some 40 fires in the Colville district; a lightning fire within 200 yards of emergency man Frank Woodruff was put out by him

Tower removed; the register, Firelookout.com and WillhiteWeb all give 1958

notes_for_editor: Height conflict: the register and Firelookout.com give 84 feet (25.6 m), which facts.height_m uses. The record's 21.3 m (70 ft) matches the July 1932 plan, and no source settles the final height. Built 1933 and removed 1958 agree across all four sources. The site's condition comes from undated WillhiteWeb text and photo captions ('Footing', 'Foundation pieces' from 2001), so nothing confirms what stands there in 2026. The summit's posted status is from WillhiteWeb only. The site is not recommended for visits. Used 1 WebSearch and 5 page reads.
